title: Linux+
description: CompTIA Linux+ XK0-006 exam prep across 5 weighted domains, with hands-on shell labs.

units.title: System Management
units.gate: Given a Linux system in an unfamiliar state, correctly identify installed packages, running services, and storage layout using only command-line tools.

objectives.text: Boot process, GRUB, and systemd targets
objectives.labPrompt: Use lsblk and df -h to map your own system's disk layout and mounted filesystems.

objectives.text: Package management across distributions (apt, dnf/yum, pacman, rpm)
Filesystem hierarchy standard and mounting/unmounting storage
Disk partitioning, LVM concepts, and filesystem types (ext4, xfs, btrfs)
systemd service management (systemctl, journalctl)
objectives.labPrompt: Use systemctl and journalctl to inspect the status and recent logs of a running service.

objectives.text: Kernel modules and basic kernel parameter tuning
Managing users, groups, and permissions at the system level

units.title: Services and User Management
units.gate: Given a multi-user Linux server scenario, correctly set up user accounts, group-based permissions, and a common network service, explaining each access-control decision.

objectives.text: Creating and managing users and groups (useradd, usermod, groups)
objectives.labPrompt: Create a new user and group on a test VM, then verify permissions with ls -l and id.

objectives.text: File permissions and ownership: rwx, chmod, chown, umask
Special permissions: SUID, SGID, sticky bit
Common network services: SSH, web servers, printing, time sync (NTP)
objectives.labPrompt: Generate an SSH key pair and configure key-based login to a test host.

objectives.text: Environment variables and shell configuration files
Print and email service basics (CUPS, mail transfer agents, conceptually)

units.title: Troubleshooting
units.gate: Given symptoms of a broken Linux system (won't boot, service down, disk full, network unreachable), diagnose root cause using systematic command-line investigation, not guesswork.

objectives.text: Systematic troubleshooting methodology for Linux systems
Diagnosing boot failures and using rescue/single-user mode
Diagnosing storage issues: full disks, inode exhaustion, failing drives
objectives.labPrompt: Use df -i and du to find what is consuming disk space or inodes on a test system.

objectives.text: Diagnosing network issues: ip, ping, traceroute, ss, DNS resolution
objectives.labPrompt: Use ss -tulpn to identify which process is listening on a given port.

objectives.text: Diagnosing performance issues: top/htop, load average, memory and swap usage
Reading and interpreting system logs for root-cause analysis

units.title: Security
units.gate: Given a freshly installed Linux server, apply a baseline hardening pass and explain what each control actually defends against.

objectives.text: User authentication hardening: password policies, sudo configuration
Firewall basics: iptables/nftables or firewalld concepts
objectives.labPrompt: Configure a basic firewalld or nftables rule to allow only SSH and HTTP on a test host.

objectives.text: SELinux/AppArmor mandatory access control concepts
File integrity and permission auditing
SSH hardening: key-only auth, disabling root login
objectives.labPrompt: Harden a test SSH server by disabling password authentication and root login.

objectives.text: Basic encryption at rest (LUKS) and in transit (TLS/SSH) concepts

units.title: Automation, Orchestration, and Scripting
units.gate: Write a short Bash script that automates a real multi-step admin task (e.g. log rotation or backup) using variables, conditionals, and a loop, and schedule it correctly.

objectives.text: Bash scripting fundamentals: variables, conditionals, loops, functions
objectives.labPrompt: Write a short Bash script that finds and archives log files older than 7 days.

objectives.text: Shell automation scheduling: cron, at, and systemd timers
Basic regular expressions with grep/sed/awk for text processing
Version control basics with git for configuration and scripts

link.note: no git command in the terminal

objectives.text: Configuration management and infrastructure-as-code concepts (Ansible-style, conceptual)
Containers: what a container is, basic Docker commands (run, ps, images)
objectives.labPrompt: Run a container image locally with docker run and inspect it with docker ps.
